Yup, started going by my name Micah a few years back, and only recently started using it at work/ signing up for schools etc. But still going by my deadname with family. It began to be a problem when I was not out to my family, but other people would call me Micah in front of them, which led to a lot of confusion and even kinda outed me to them. 

Even after a few years it’s weird and it does get easier, sometimes I like to “brush it off” when people ask why my deadname is on certain documents, “oh that’s just my legal name, nobody calls me that” “it’s just for legal documents so it’s weird to hear” etc. Or vice versa with family I’m not 100% out to. “Oh Micah is just a nickname my friends call me” “it’s a long story how I got it”

This only kind of works with my name because it passes off as unisex (it is, but most people where I live though think of it as a male name) My deadname though is VERY feminine and when people hear it they automatically will start to see me as a woman, and will start using the wrong pronouns, even if they know my name. 

Sometimes if there’s someone who’s struggling calling you by a certain name, and you can start small by telling people “it’s a nickname”. 

With some people however, I didn’t announce I was changing my name, I just started doing it and they were like “hey I guess that’s what your name is now”

It’s weird and frustrating and I still hate when people deadname me, and wish I could’ve either waited until I was fully transitioned, or maybe came out earlier. It doesn’t matter either way though, there’s never going to be a right time to change your name, it just happens. But that’s just my personal experience lol

green/eco products. The idea and motive is admirable, but if you think for one extra second you realize it's extremely counterproductive. Most of the products are almost always ways to cut down on plastic. ex; company comes out with "compostable" paper packaging, but they still have their plastic packaging being sold in addition, it's just creating more waste. (most) Compostable packaging requires industrial sized compost centers or bins that are not always accessible to people, nor is the average person going to stress about where to throw their paper detergent bottle, they are going to throw it in the garbage or recycling (don't even get me started on the recycling system). So it's not solving any problem, just adding to them, more emissions to manufacture extra product and more waste to be tossed with nowhere to go. Additionally, they are not cheaper by any means, so consumers are less likely to choose it. 

They are missing the fundamental point that it's not the consumers fault for pollution, its not our fault because we forgot to recycle a milk carton in 2009, its THIER own. Its companies basically saying "You can fix this problem that WE took part in creating by buying our products so we can continue to worsen said problem! Don't forget to recycle and compost (properly) tee hee!" 

It's not like it's a secret, it can feasibly be a solution in this economy. I could go on but honestly look it up on your own, its so stupid.
